Parallel and cluster runs¶

This chapter covers what goes beyond a run on one Linux machine: parallel runs on Windows, how well Priroda scales, and job scripts for batch systems. Starting a parallel run on Linux is described in Installing and running, and the resource limits that apply to every process in Keeping scratch in memory and the sections around it.

Parallel performance¶

What is known about parallel performance:

  • DFT speeds up within one node; reports differ on how far. One user found in 2016 that beyond 6–8 cores the gain is at most about 10%, even for large systems such as (C60)9. Another measured a 38-step optimization of a small molecule at 101, 63 and 37 s on single nodes with 8, 12 and 24 cores. A small PBE/L1 optimization with version 10 took 81.5, 42.5, 29.8 and 29.3 s on 1–4 cores. In a version 25 test, a numerical ridft Hessian of water took 4.9 s on 2 processes instead of 7.2 s. An optimization plus analytic Hessian of a 22-atom copper complex (OLYP/L2, fine grid) took 32 min on 8 processes of one node; on one process it had not finished after an hour.

  • Parallel results equal serial ones in version 25 tests. On 2 processes, a water energy and a numerical ridft Hessian gave exactly the serial numbers. In version 6, results were reported to differ in the last digits between runs on different numbers of processes, and an unstable TS search once followed different paths for different -np.

  • Running across nodes gives no gain for DFT. Use one node per DFT job. RI-MP2 is the exception: the version 8 benchmark under Keeping scratch in memory ran 6 times faster on 4 nodes with scratch in RAM than on 2 cores of one node.

  • Memory per process does not drop when you add processes, and in a parallel Hessian nearly all of the disk use is on rank 0.

  • RI-MP2 parallelizes better than DFT, according to one user “at least in memory”. The version 5 documentation limits useful parallelism to Nproc ≤ min(N_atoms, N_occ) and recommends a number of processes that divides the number of occupied orbitals nearly evenly. For N_occ = 14 it rates 2, 7 or 14 processes as best, 3 or 5 as acceptable, 6 as poor and 13 as very bad.

  • Small RI jobs on many processes can hang (reported in 2015; not tested in version 25). RI-MP2 and RI-DFT hang with no message when a process receives no work. The output then shows a line 0 blocks ... on node N after integral estimates. Run small RI jobs on one or a few cores.

  • Several independent jobs often beat one parallel job. On a 4-core machine in 2009, for jobs not limited by disk, four single-core jobs ran about 30% faster in total than the same jobs run one after another on 4 cores each.

Older versions scaled worse. In version 6 a parallel Hessian could use at most 2 cores and could hang on 4, and a version 7 MP2 run crashed (signal 8) on more than about 24 cores. Use version 17 or later for parallel work.

Hangs, crashes and poor speed-up in parallel runs are covered in Parallel and MPI problems.

Batch systems¶

Priroda needs nothing special from a batch system. The job script has to:

  1. request one node and the number of cores you will use (for RI-MP2, see parallel performance);

  2. point the scratch to the node’s local disk or to RAM, by exporting TMPDIR or by path= in $system;

  3. make the memory request cover memory + |negative disk| for every process;

  4. start Priroda with the input and output file names.

This Slurm script was tested in version 25 on a single-node Slurm 23.11. Directory names and module setup are site-specific.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=mol
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=8
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00

PRIRODA=$HOME/priroda/p                      # full path to the executable
cd "$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR"
export TMPDIR=/local/scratch/$SLURM_JOB_ID   # node-local disk; site-specific
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"

env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" TMPDIR="$TMPDIR" \
  $HOME/priroda/mpiexec -np "$SLURM_NTASKS" "$PRIRODA" mol.in mol.out   # the mpiexec from the official site
status=$?

rm -rf "$TMPDIR"
exit $status

Two lines matter more than they look:

  • env -i. The mpiexec from the official site refuses to start when the environment holds 193 or more variables. It prints Environment is too large (max is 193) and exits, and Priroda never runs. A Slurm job easily has that many, because Slurm adds its own SLURM_* variables; in the test, a job inherited 210 and the unmodified script failed this way. env -i starts mpiexec with only the variables listed.

  • exit $status. Without it the job’s exit status is that of rm, so Slurm reports a failed run as COMPLETED. This is what happened in the test above.

When a job is cancelled (scancel) or reaches its time limit, Slurm sends signal 15 (SIGTERM). Priroda then writes process 0 got signal 15 and then process 0 got signal 2 to the output, deletes its own scratch files, and stops; Slurm’s own log file says CANCELLED or CANCELLED ... DUE TO TIME LIMIT. The rm at the end of the script does not run, so the empty scratch directory stays. To remove it as well, set the clean-up as a trap before starting Priroda: replace the lines of the script from env -i through exit $status with these.

trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR"' EXIT
trap 'exit 143' TERM
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" TMPDIR="$TMPDIR" \
  $HOME/priroda/mpiexec -np "$SLURM_NTASKS" "$PRIRODA" mol.in mol.out &
wait $!

Two jobs of one process each ran side by side on the same node without trouble, each with its own scratch directory.

Under PBS/Torque the same steps read the number of cores from $PBS_NODEFILE. This script was not tested; it uses env -i and exit $status for the same reasons as the Slurm one. Some PBS sites (e.g. KNC) provide a per-job local scratch directory and delete it after the job.

#!/bin/bash
#PBS -N mol
#PBS -l nodes=1:ppn=8,walltime=24:00:00

cd "$PBS_O_WORKDIR"
NP=$(wc -l < "$PBS_NODEFILE")
export TMPDIR=/local/scratch/$PBS_JOBID      # site-specific
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"

env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" TMPDIR="$TMPDIR" \
  $HOME/priroda/mpiexec -np "$NP" $HOME/priroda/p mol.in mol.out
status=$?

rm -rf "$TMPDIR"
exit $status

If /tmp on the node is small or has a quota, a large job dies writing a scratch file, for example 0: write file /tmp/tmp9633.11 (leAX): .... Point the scratch at the cluster’s scratch file system or at RAM.

Historical: the KNC wrappers. The Kazan Scientific Centre clusters (2006–2012) provided the wrappers pbspriroda5, pbspriroda5-mpi and pbspriroda6, called as pbspriroda6 file_name -time hh:mm:ss -queue queue -mem MB -disk size -procs 1:ppn=N. The wrappers wrote the $system group themselves from -mem and -disk, so inputs submitted through them had to omit $system. Forum posts and old FAQs that mention these commands refer to that site only.

A run killed with signal 15 alone (for example by timeout or kill) ends its output with process 0 got signal 15 and no further message; under Slurm a process 0 got signal 2 line follows, as described above. Give long jobs enough wall time: in a version 25 test, the analytic Hessian of a 22-atom copper complex with L2 basis and a fine grid did not finish within an hour on one core, after a 6-step optimization that had taken most of that hour.

Parallel runs on Windows¶

The official site shows this command for a two-process run:

mpirun.exe -np 2 p.exe C60.qm.in C60.qm.w.2.out

The current index has no p.exe: use p_190306.exe in place of p.exe, here and in the commands below.

The MPI runtime is not on the site. Users assembled it from Cygwin as follows:

  1. Download the 64-bit Cygwin installer (setup-x86_64.exe from https://cygwin.com). Install the default packages plus the openmpi package.

  2. Copy these files from the Cygwin installation into the directory with the Priroda executable: cygwin1.dll, cyggcc_s-seh-1.dll, cygmpi-12.dll, cygopen-pal-13.dll, cygopen-rte-12.dll, orterun.exe. Take cygwin1.dll from the same installation, because the other DLLs work only with matching versions. After this, Cygwin itself is no longer needed.

  3. Create a directory dev one level above the directory that holds cygwin1.dll, with subdirectories shm and mqueue. For Priroda in C:\Priroda, that means C:\dev\shm and C:\dev\mqueue. The Cygwin libraries take the parent of the directory that holds cygwin1.dll as the root /: with the DLL in C:\Priroda, C:\Users is /Users.

  4. If the program is in a system directory such as C:\Program Files, run it as administrator.

  5. Set TMPDIR and start the run from cmd.exe, giving the path of the Priroda executable with forward slashes:

    cd /d C:\Work
set "TMPDIR=%TEMP%"
C:\Priroda\orterun.exe -np 2 C:/Priroda/p_190306.exe file.in file.out

Important

p_190306.exe needs exactly the files cygmpi-12.dll, cygopen-pal-13.dll and cygopen-rte-12.dll. Current Cygwin OpenMPI packages ship cygmpi-40.dll, cygopen-pal-40.dll and cygopen-rte-40.dll instead. With those, or with those copied under the old names, the program and orterun.exe exit at once with code -1073741515 (0xC0000135, a required DLL was not found), and nothing is printed. A test in 2026 worked with the -12/-13 files and orterun.exe from an older OpenMPI package (files dated 2016-06-21). Take orterun.exe from the same package as the DLLs.

To get the old files, install Cygwin from an archived snapshot instead of the current one. The Cygwin installation page (https://cygwin.com/install.html) lists archived snapshots for old Windows versions. The 2016 x86_64 snapshot there worked:

setup-x86_64.exe --allow-unsupported-windows --no-verify --site http://ctm.crouchingtigerhiddenfruitbat.org/pub/cygwin/circa/64bit/2016/08/30/104235

Select the openmpi package, then copy the files listed in step 2 from the bin directory of that installation.

That test ran on Windows 10 with the old Cygwin installed. p_190306.exe then printed parallel on 2 processors and gave the same energy as a serial run. With a backslash path to the executable (C:\Priroda\p_190306.exe), orterun.exe stopped with orterun:exe-not-found. Started directly, without orterun.exe, p_190306.exe runs serially.

Problems reported with this setup:

  • The recipe needs a Priroda build that supports parallel runs. Version 6 (p6.exe) failed with an OpenMPI agent-not-found error; the user was advised to use version 17 or later.

  • On a computer connected by Wi-Fi that also has a wired network adapter, OpenMPI stops with tcp_peer_send_blocking: send() to socket 12 failed: Transport endpoint is not connected (128). Disable the wired adapter.

  • With the Ethernet cable unplugged, one user’s run used only two of the cores.

  • Warning: '/dev/shm' does not exists or is not a directory. means the Cygwin environment is missing. Create the dev directories (step 3), or start from a Cygwin shell.

A user reported in 2021 that this recipe no longer worked on Windows 10 with a current Cygwin, and no fix was posted. The likely cause is the newer OpenMPI DLLs described above. The serial build was tested on a PC without Cygwin; the parallel run was tested only with the old Cygwin installed.
